title: Chicken Tikka Masala
subtitle: British-Indian grilled chicken in creamy tomato masala sauce
excerpt: Chicken tikka masala is Britain's most widely eaten curry: charred pieces of marinated chicken in a rich, creamy tomato sauce spiced with garam masala, cumin, and ginger. It is a British creation, developed in Indian restaurants in Britain in the 1970s, and is now one of the most popular dishes in the world. When made well at home, it is outstanding.
sourceNotes: Chicken tikka masala is considered by many to be Britain's national dish. It was created in Indian restaurants in Britain in the 1970s, most likely by Bangladeshi chefs adapting tikka (marinated grilled chicken) to British tastes by adding a creamy tomato sauce. The dish is distinct from any dish in India, though it has influenced Indian restaurant menus worldwide.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in the sauce. Reheat gently.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The marinade can go on the night before. The sauce can be made a day ahead.

content.text: The char on the chicken is essential -- without it, the dish lacks its defining smoky-sweet quality. Grill the chicken under a very hot grill until it chars at the edges, then add it to the sauce. Do not skip this step. The marinade should go on for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.

items.prepNote: boneless, skinless, cut into 4 cm pieces

content.text: Mix {{yoghurt-full-fat}} yoghurt with {{cumin-ground}} cumin, {{coriander-ground}} coriander, {{turmeric-ground}} turmeric, and {{chilli-flakes}} chilli. Add grated {{garlic}} garlic, {{ginger-root}} ginger, and {{salt-table}} salt. Toss {{chicken-thigh}} chicken in the marinade. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

Thread marinated chicken onto skewers or spread on a foil-lined baking tray. Grill under a very hot grill at 220C for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through. Set aside.

Heat {{vegetable-oil}} oil and {{unsalted-butter}} butter in a large pan. Cook {{onion}} onion for 10 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic and {{ginger-root}} ginger. Cook for 2 minutes. Add {{garam-masala}} garam masala, {{cumin-ground}} cumin, {{smoked-paprika}} smoked paprika, and {{tomato-puree}} tomato puree. Stir for 1 minute. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tomatoes. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add {{double-cream}} cream. Simmer for 5 minutes. Add the grilled chicken and simmer for 5 more minutes. Taste for {{salt-table}} salt. Serve with basmati rice and naan.

items.symptom: The sauce is very acidic and sharp
items.cause: The tomatoes need more cooking time.
items.fix: Simmer the sauce uncovered for 5 to 10 more minutes. The acidity softens as the tomatoes cook. A small pinch of sugar also helps balance the sauce if it remains sharp.

content.text: Chicken tikka masala was most likely created in Indian restaurants in Glasgow or London in the 1970s and 1980s. The exact origin is disputed, but the dish is clearly a British creation. It was voted Britain's favourite dish in multiple surveys in the 1990s and 2000s. Foreign Secretary Robin Cook famously described it as a true British national dish in 2001 -- a dish that represents Britain's openness to new influences.
